title: Common-stage derived direct image and induced Weil adjunction

source.place: Existing landed interface, lines 275-480; sources recorded there: Bhatt-Scholze 6.8.14(2), 6.8.15 and Stacks 099N, 0D6G, 05TE. Reindexed from def-weil-derived-direct-image, not a new mathematical claim.

statement: Fix a finite-field datum D, a prime l distinct from its characteristic, an algebraic closure Omega of Q_l, and a morphism f:X_0 to Y_0 of finite-type quasi-compact models over the base field [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. On their geometric fibres use the actual common-stage constructible categories [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] and the normalized derived pullback [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. The finite/integral direct-image construction is [def-weil-derived-direct-image]. The common-stage pullback has a right adjoint sfModelDerivedPush, with its specified adjunction sfModelDerivedAdjunction. Pullback composition, with the normalized composition comparison and Frobenius square specified in [def-zl-weil-ind-sheaf-category], gives the normalized commuting-square comparison, whose adjoint is sfModelDerivedExchange; the derived adjunction gives the compatible direct-image shift comparison and the image of connecting morphisms. Frobenius pullback is an equivalence. Its normalized square lifts this adjunction to the actual Weil fixed-pair categories [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], defining sfModelWeilDerivedPush and sfModelWeilDerivedAdjunction. Forgetting the Weil structure identifies this right adjoint with sfModelDerivedPush by the unique natural isomorphism whose image under geometric pullback, followed by the geometric counit, is the carrier of the Weil counit. These constructions are exactly the already-landed declarations of Sheaf.Paper.SfCommonStageDirectImage; no claim of arbitrary-field Weil models or of new finite-reduction comparison isomorphisms is added.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal C=\mathcal C_Y$, $\mathcal D=\mathcal C_X$ for the actual common-stage categories. Apply [lem-sf-rational-direct-image-adjunctions] to $f_0$. At coefficient stages $i\le j$ write $S_{ij}$ for extension on $Y$, $T_{ij}$ for extension on $X$, $L_i\dashv R_i$ for the stage adjunction, $c_{ij}:L_jS_{ij}\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{ij}L_i$ for the left comparison, and $b_{ij}:S_{ij}R_i\xrightarrow{\sim}R_jT_{ij}$ for the right comparison. With usual right-to-left composition its stated mate equation is $\varepsilon_j\circ L_j(b_{ij})=T_{ij}(\varepsilon_i)\circ c_{ij,R_i}$. These are rational constructible adjunctions, not arbitrary ambient sheaf adjunctions.

proof.text: Check unit compatibility by the stage-$j$ Hom bijection. The transposes of $b_{ij,L_iK}\circ S_{ij}(\eta_{i,K})$ and $R_j(c_{ij,K})\circ\eta_{j,S_{ij}K}$ are both $c_{ij,K}$: for the first, substitute the mate equation, move $S_{ij}(\eta_i)$ past $c_{ij}$ by naturality, and cancel $\varepsilon_iL_i\circ L_i\eta_i=1$; for the second cancel the stage-$j$ triangle identity. Thus the units form a compatible family. The counit compatibility is the given mate equation itself.

source.place: DirectImageAdjunction and rationalStageAdjunction_descends, lines 39–237; public constructors lines 275–480; Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 6.8.14(2), Remark 6.8.15.

proof.text: For $i\le j\le k$, the two composites from $S_{jk}S_{ij}R_i$ to $R_kT_{ik}$ are $R_k(t_{ijk})\circ b_{jk,T_{ij}}\circ S_{jk}(b_{ij})$ and $b_{ik}\circ s_{ijk,R_i}$, where $s,t$ are the stage associators. Apply the injective inverse Hom bijection for $L_k\dashv R_k$. Substituting the mate equation twice in the first composite gives $t_{ijk}\circ T_{jk}T_{ij}(\varepsilon_i)\circ T_{jk}(c_{ij,R_i})\circ c_{jk,S_{ij}R_i}$. Naturality of $t$ and coherence of $c$ identify this with $T_{ik}(\varepsilon_i)\circ c_{ik,R_i}\circ L_k(s_{ijk,R_i})$, the transpose of the second composite. Hence the right comparisons are coherent. The identity comparison follows by the same transposition with $i=j$, giving the unit constraint. No new geometric assertion enters this calculation.

source.place: DirectImageAdjunction and rationalStageAdjunction_descends, lines 39–237; public constructors lines 275–480; Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 6.8.14(2), Remark 6.8.15.

proof.text: Construct the right functor directly on the actual pair category [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]: send $(i,K)$ to $(i,R_iK)$ and a representative $u:T_{im}K\to T_{jm}K'$ to $b_{jm,K'}^{-1}\circ R_m(u)\circ b_{im,K}$. Refining the representative gives the same class, by naturality of $b$ and the coherence equation proved in step 3. Identity and composition follow by $b^{-1}b=1$ at a common stage. Represent each unit and counit by its component at the object's stage; step 2 gives their naturality across stages. The two triangle composites are identities at every finite stage, hence identities as classes. The descended left functor equals the prescribed common-stage pullback: on $(E,K)$ it is $(E,Lf_E^*K)$, and on a representative $u$ over $M$ it is the conjugate $\beta_{\mathrm{target}}^{-1}Lf_M^*(u)\beta_{\mathrm{source}}$ in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. This specifies an adjunction on the actual pair category. Define sfModelDerivedPush as a right adjoint selected from this universal property, and sfModelDerivedAdjunction as its adjunction. The universal property, rather than unspecified object choices, determines its data.

source.place: DirectImageAdjunction and rationalStageAdjunction_descends, lines 39–237; public constructors lines 275–480; Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 6.8.14(2), Remark 6.8.15.

proof.text: Use the normalized composition comparison specified on rationalized integral representatives in [def-zl-weil-ind-sheaf-category]. It gives $L(gf)^*\cong Lf^*Lg^*$ on geometric common-stage categories. For a commuting square $jb=aj_W$, composing this comparison, the equality of composites, and its inverse gives $\theta:Lj_W^*La^*\xrightarrow{\sim}Lb^*Lj^*$. Define the exchange on $K$ as the adjunct of $Lj_W^*La^*Rj_*K\xrightarrow{\theta}Lb^*Lj^*Rj_*K\xrightarrow{Lb^*(\varepsilon_j)}Lb^*K$. This is exactly sfModelPullComposition, sfModelPullSquare and sfModelDerivedExchange. Naturality follows by applying the natural Hom bijection to this natural composite.

source.place: DirectImageAdjunction and rationalStageAdjunction_descends, lines 39–237; public constructors lines 275–480; Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 6.8.14(2), Remark 6.8.15.

proof.text: The specified pullback commutes with shifts; this follows by its finite/integral/rational/common-stage construction in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and by descent of the finite-stage shift comparisons in [prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors]. Apply clause (iii) of [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-shift-compatibility-unique] to the geometric adjunction: it supplies the unique shift structure on its right adjoint compatible with its unit and counit. For $w:K\to L[1]$, define its connecting-map image by $R(w)$ followed by this specified comparison $R(L[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}(RL)[1]$. These are sfModelPushCommShift and sfModelPushConnecting, including the shift comparison rather than just the unshifted image.

source.place: DirectImageAdjunction and rationalStageAdjunction_descends, lines 39–237; public constructors lines 275–480; Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 6.8.14(2), Remark 6.8.15.

proof.text: Each geometric fibre is finite type over $k$ by base-change stability [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. Since a field is Noetherian, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] gives Noetherianity; [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] gives finite topological Krull dimension. In every residue field the image of $\ell\ne p$ is nonzero, hence invertible. The local-ring residue criterion gives stalk invertibility: if $uv-1$ is in the maximal ideal for a lift $v$ of the residue inverse of $u=\ell$, then $uv$ and hence $u$ are units. Thus the hypotheses of the coefficient comparison and common-stage identity theorems are satisfied, including the empty fibre.

source.place: DirectImageAdjunction and rationalStageAdjunction_descends, lines 39–237; public constructors lines 275–480; Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 6.8.14(2), Remark 6.8.15.

proof.text: Take the simultaneous comparison system given by [lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison], and apply [lem-sf-common-stage-pullback-identity] on each fibre. Geometric Frobenius $g_X$ is a scheme automorphism with the explicitly specified inverse [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. The normalized pullback compositions of step 5, followed by this identity comparison, identify $Lg_X^*L(g_X^{-1})^*$ and $L(g_X^{-1})^*Lg_X^*$ with the identity. They exhibit $Lg_X^*$ as an equivalence. For $f_0$ over $k_0$, $g_Yf=fg_X$: both have the same projection to the model and act on the field factor by the same $\gamma$; the fibre-product universal property proves equality. Composing the normalized composition comparisons along this equality gives $e:L G\xrightarrow{\sim}F L$, for $L=Lf^*$, $F=Lg_Y^*$ and $G=Lg_X^*$, with diagrammatic juxtaposition: $LG=G\circ L$ and $FL=L\circ F$. This is the prescribed Frobenius square.

source.place: DirectImageAdjunction and rationalStageAdjunction_descends, lines 39–237; public constructors lines 275–480; Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 6.8.14(2), Remark 6.8.15.

proof.text: Form $b:RF\to GR$ (diagrammatic, i.e. $F\circ R\to R\circ G$ with components $FRM\to RGM$) as the mate of $e^{-1}:FL\to LG$ (i.e. $L\circ F\to G\circ L$), where $R=$sfModelDerivedPush. Apply [lem-weil-mate-iso-along-equivalences] to $L\dashv R$ on both sides, with horizontal functors $F,G$. They are equivalences by step 8, so its hypotheses (source equivalence and target fully faithful) hold; therefore $b$ is invertible. Apply [lem-sf-fixed-pair-adjunction-lift] to $e,b$. Its carrier adjunction is exactly the geometric one. The actual Weil-complex categories are precisely these fixed-pair categories [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Select its right adjoint and adjunction to define sfModelWeilDerivedPush and sfModelWeilDerivedAdjunction. This uses no derived category of Weil sheaves and no ind-category.

source.place: DirectImageAdjunction and rationalStageAdjunction_descends, lines 39–237; public constructors lines 275–480; Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 6.8.14(2), Remark 6.8.15.

proof.text: Let $\widetilde R$ be the selected Weil right adjoint and $R^W$ the explicit lifted right adjoint of step 9, with counits $\widetilde\varepsilon,\varepsilon^W$. For each Weil pair $K$, take the transpose under $L^W\dashv R^W$ of $\widetilde\varepsilon_K:L^W\widetilde RK\to K$. Transposition in the other adjunction gives its inverse: both composites are identities since their transposes are the relevant counits. These component maps are natural by naturality of counits and Hom bijections. Forgetting yields an isomorphism $u:\operatorname{For}_Y\widetilde R\xrightarrow{\sim}R\operatorname{For}_X$ with $\varepsilon_{\operatorname{For}_XK}\circ L(u_K)=\operatorname{For}_X(\widetilde\varepsilon_K)$, because the lifted counit has geometric carrier by [lem-sf-fixed-pair-adjunction-lift]. If $v$ satisfies this same equation, injectivity of the geometric inverse Hom bijection gives $u_K=v_K$ for every $K$, hence equality of natural isomorphisms. This constructs and uniquely normalizes sfModelWeilDerivedPushForget.

lean.note: The recorded SfIntegralDirectImage supplies only the completed integral reduction tower. This module publicly retains that construction and extends it to the actual geometric common-stage category and its induced Weil pairs by the inverse-image adjunction. The forgetful comparison is uniquely normalized by its counit; shift and open-exchange comparisons use the prescribed pullback comparisons.
